Describe the following in detail:

Interface

Interfaces create a connection between a package component and a component outside of the package. External interface specifications list all external applications, databases and hardware devices that need to communicate with the package. The details on how the functionality should be developed are detailed in this specification.

Extensions

Extensions are enhancements, modifications or bolt-ons that require custom coding. The way the transaction is performed will be changed and will no longer be considered standard package functionality. The details on how the functionality should be developed are detailed in this specification. These are typically developed either by modifying the source code of the package or by using the scripting capability that is provided with the package.

Package extension can be:

  1. User interface enhancements (e.g., adding a new textbox)
  2. Batch enhancements (e.g., changing the interest accruals formula)
  3. Database changes (e.g., adding a new Oracle database Table)

Interface enhancements:

The following parameters are identified for each user interface design:

  • Field - field name
  • Data - data required
  • Calculations - define any calculations or formulas
  • Drop-down - define all drop-down lists
  • Default data - identify special or unique processes, functions, fields or actions
  • Font name and style - font name and regular, bold, bold italic or italic
  • Font color and size - define color code and point size
  • Rules - any special rules governing development
  • Pop-up messages - define action and content of popup messages
  • Formats - date and time formats
  • Events - define next event to occur

Batch enhancements:

The following parameters are identified for each user batch run unit:

  • Batch job dependencies
  • Interfaces that monitor the execution of the batch
  • Package batch execution environment
  • Status elements on whether a batch was run successfully, or an error has occurred

Database changes:

The following parameters are identified for database changes:

  • Functionality - definition, performance, management, utilities, archiving, metadata, etc.
  • Security - parameters and access controls and reporting
  • Quality - data quality controls and reporting
  • Integration - extract-transform-load (ETL) process and reporting

Forms

Forms display information to support business processes. They are customizations to the standard package that require custom coding. The details on how the functionality should be developed are detailed in this specification.

Workflows

Business workflows are customizations to the standard package that require custom coding. The details on how the functionality should be developed are detailed in this specification.

The following should be considered when designing the workflow:

  • A complete set of procedures or steps
  • Detailed inputs and outputs
  • Data flows
  • Decision branches
  • Automated rules

Screen Layout and Flow Design

Create solution screen layouts and screen flows for the identified objects for the stakeholders to visualize and confirm the proposed graphical user interface (GUI), screen flow and navigation.
To describe in detail how the package should be developed to meet requirements.
